item.title: How AI could make it harder for governments to use hacking tools
item.description: AI is proving effective at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. Some say this will make it harder for governments to use hacking tools and spyware and could reignite calls to backdoor devices.

item.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
item.description: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.

item.title: Amazon hikes hardware prices by 60%, blaming memory shortage
item.description: As the memory shortage continues to cause trouble for hardware makers, Amazon says it is now being forced to pass on the costs to its consumers.

item.title: Apple is reportedly cutting hundreds of jobs from Siri, Vision Pro teams
item.description: Apple has admitted that some roles are being impacted as it shifts its focus away from certain initiatives.

item.title: AI data giant Alation confirms cyberattack
item.description: The data search and AI giant confirmed unauthorized access to its systems during an incident on Tuesday, and said it was investigating the breach.

item.title: AI was supposed to win people over by now — it hasn’t
item.description: As AI becomes harder to avoid, consumers are growing more wary of the technology — and Silicon Valley is discovering that widespread adoption doesn’t necessarily lead to acceptance.

item.title: Chinese AI model Kimi escaped its cybersecurity testing environment, researchers say
item.description: In the Kimi test, the sandbox designed to contain the experiment was not properly configured.

item.title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others

item.title: Anthropic’s new Claude feature is quietly selling you on AI
item.description: Claude’s new Reflect dashboard doesn’t just visualize how you use AI. It also subtly reinforces how much of your daily work now depends on Anthropic’s chatbot.

item.title: Meta wants its AI glasses to seem less creepy. Its AI strategy says otherwise.
item.description: Meta is adding a new safeguard to stop people from secretly recording others with its AI glasses. But the update comes as the company continues to expand how much personal data its AI products collect and use.

item.title: OpenAI releases new voice models for more natural live conversations
